channel.title: this.live blog
channel.description: Building a one-person software and AI practice in public, with receipts.

item.title: The cron that died quietly
item.description: A scheduled job can stop running for two months without anything telling you it stopped. Here is how my weekly blog cron went quiet and what I changed.

item.title: The first thing my marketing agent produced is not allowed to send itself
item.description: A four touch outbound sequence, written by an agent, landed marked draft only with four named blockers standing between it and a single email.

item.title: An outside audit cut my animation timings in half and it was right
item.description: A motion audit from someone who does this for a living took my banner animation from 1.8 seconds to 0.8 and changed two repositories in a day.

item.title: There was a daemon running on my main machine that nothing documented
item.description: I wrote a runbook for a process that had been running on my primary workstation with no owner, no documentation and no way for anyone else to touch it.

item.title: Nine projects were carrying real work that had never left this machine
item.description: On one day I committed local working state in nine repositories.

item.title: The most useful thing I shipped that week was an accurate description of work already done
item.description: A thin week on the fleet.

item.title: I took myself out of the approval path for a system that writes its own tools
item.description: On 2026-08-01 I removed the per-skill human gate from the autonomous learning loop and replaced it with policy, receipts, automatic demotion and a kill file.

item.title: The quality bar I ratified failed first on my own page
item.description: I ratified a quality bar on a Tuesday.

item.title: A release nobody is allowed to cut is not a release
item.description: Three fail-closed gates landed in one week.

item.title: What 14 principles taught me about operating as one person
item.description: I had 14 founder principles. I cut them to 9. The compression taught me about what actually guides decisions when you are the only person building.

item.title: How I moved one idea through every surface I own
item.description: A conceptual shift cascaded through the philosophy page, landing copy, pillar cards, animations, and resume in a single week. This is about how consistency works when one person owns everything.

item.title: The receipt convention keeps the work honest
item.description: Every consequential agent action writes a short note. A daily job reads the notes and a one-page summary goes to Telegram with coffee. Here is why that system exists.

item.title: The agnostic cheat code
item.description: Your own local memory is the substrate that survives every model change, every surface change, every dispatch change. Mnemos is the proof.
